name: Memory
summary: How an AI application remembers beyond one call: short-term memory in the context window, long-term memory in stores it saves to and searches.

D1.guide: Guess first: does the model itself remember yesterday's chat?
text: The AI forgets everything when a chat ends. To remember you, the app writes notes in a notebook.
Next time, it reads the useful notes back to the AI before you start talking.
D1.analogy: A notebook the helper reads before each visit.

text: The model's weights do not change while you chat, so all memory lives in the application.
**Short-term memory** is the conversation inside the context window. When it gets too long, older turns are dropped or **summarised**.
**Long-term memory** is a store outside the model: facts, preferences and past summaries saved to a file or database, then searched and loaded back into the context when relevant.
D2.analogy: A notebook the helper reads before each visit.
D2.analogyBreaks: A person decides what is worth writing down and notices when a note is out of date. An AI memory system can save wrong or stale facts, or even planted instructions, and then trust them later.

predict.question: A chat app remembers your name in a new conversation. Where is that memory most likely kept?
options: Inside the model's weights, updated as you chat
In a store the app saved to, loaded back into the prompt
In the GPU's cache from last week
predict.explanation: Weights are fixed at inference time. The app saves facts outside the model and puts them back into the context window when a new chat starts.

text: Hard parts: deciding what to save and what to forget, keeping memories correct as facts change, and stopping injected text from becoming a lasting memory.
Summaries lose detail, and there is no agreed way yet to test whether long-term memory makes an assistant better or just more confident.

sources.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
